title: Client drain handshake, prefetch reconciliation, and partial-generation cleanup
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem statement: When clients disconnect mid-generation (network blips, tab close, SDK-level cancellation), the runtime currently either preserves too much state (wasting memory and KV TTLs) or drops in-flight partial outputs immediately, causing inconsistent behaviors for downstream structured outputs and function-calls. We need a clear, measurable drain/handshake + prefetch reconciliation protocol that: 1) gives well-scoped time for clients to reconnect and complete function-call handoffs; 2) reconciles prefetched KV cache state vs committed prefixes to avoid double-prefetch or incorrect cache poisoning; 3) garbage-collects partial generations according to policy tiers without risking user-visible breakage for short reconnect windows.
acceptance_criteria: Introduce a client-side drain-handshake RPC that marks intent-to-abandon and returns a resumable token when applicable
Runtime honors a configurable grace window (default 30s for hosted, 120s for dedicated) before full GC of partial generations
Prefetch reconciliation step prevents duplicate prefetch on resume (idempotent prefetch), and stale KV entries produced by abandoned partials are not exposed to later generations
Function-call invocations that started during a generation are either completed atomically or rolled back consistently with structured-output contracts
End-to-end tests cover disconnect during token streaming, disconnect right after function call emission, and rapid reconnect within grace window
Relevant observability exposed: per-request life_cycle (started|drain_handshake|quarantine|gc), metrics for grace-window hits/misses, and alert when GC rate spikes > 3x baseline
rollout_plan: Feature flag behind runtime config: streaming.client_drain_handshake (default off)
Stage 1: Canary in non-prod and internal stack; collect telemetry for 7 days
Stage 2: Enable for 5% of hosted traffic and all Dedicated customers who opt-in
Stage 3: Ramp to 50% after 48h stable telemetry, then full rollout with docs and SDK updates
Fallback: automatic immediate GC on timeout if memory pressure high, documented as a behavior under heavy load
test_plan: Unit tests for drain handshake state transitions (STARTED -> DRAIN_HANDSHAKE -> QUARANTINE -> GC)
Integration test: simulated flaky client that disconnects at random offsets and reconnects within grace window; verify resume token validity and no duplicate tokens emitted
Chaos test: kill worker during prefetch reconciliation to validate idempotency and recovery
Regression: function-call emission followed by disconnect should not leave dangling external calls (use mock tool endpoints)
risks: Extended grace windows increase memory/KV retention — mitigated via per-account limits and adaptive eviction under pressure
Function-call atomicity complexity: some third-party tool calls are not idempotent — we will require SDK/tooling best-effort adapters and document non-idempotent tool behavior
Latency overhead from additional reconciliation step when resuming — measure and optimize hot paths; provide opt-out per customer

2025-02-18 Design feedback (Ana Ruiz): Ask to ensure structured-output schema includes a `resumption_cursor` to allow SDKs to decide whether to retry or escalate to fresh request.
